scientific_interpretation: This slice confirms that EXP-F is functioning as a falsification experiment rather than a confirmation test: replay and malformed-event escape paths were exposed, repaired, converted into deterministic regressions, and verified on the exact repaired SHA. It does not establish overall governance correctness because most pre-registered EXP-F attack classes remain unexecuted.
required_next_step: Continue EXP-F against the remaining registered attack classes, especially stale/forged provenance, cross-project/task event binding, concurrent completion races, forbidden corrective scope, budget/resource exhaustion semantics, normalized-finding loss, canonical evidence identity, and COMPLETE promotion. Do not declare EXP-F complete from this slice.
limitations: The four cases are deterministic governor regressions, not independent model-review cases.
This slice covers replay consumption and malformed event structures only; it does not measure the full EXP-F attack surface.
Passing regressions prove the repaired paths at the exact execution SHA, not absence of other governance defects.
No population-level reliability threshold is inferred from four adversarial cases.
